messages:
ellie_support: Hey team — urgent escalation from customer ACME (internal ticket #8894). They deployed after the weekend rollout and say a previously reliable assistant now refuses to include short lists in its answers and instead returns a single paragraph. Customer pasted before/after outputs. Says behavior started right after the 2026-03-15 deploy. Can eng/ML triage? :warning:

mike_eng: tagging @sara_ml & @jamal_prod. Do we have any recent tokenizer or chat-template changes in the rollout?

sara_ml: we merged two small changes in the rollout: (1) tokenizer update to normalize unicode and treat consecutive newlines as a single separator, (2) chat template trimming of trailing whitespace in system prompt. Both in commit abc123 and rolled to stable-2026-03-15. Noted we also toggled include_eos_on_prompt=true for a subset of models.

ellie_support: customer provided repro. Minimal curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-vicuna-1.2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"List the top 3 reasons to prefer X over Y:\n- speed\n- cost\n- support"}],"temperature":0.0}'
```
They said OLD (pre-rollout) output was a 3-bullet list matching the input formatting. NEW output after rollout: a single paragraph listing reasons inline. They also captured tokenization diff with our tokenizer before/after:

OLD tokenized prompt tail: 
[... , '\n', '-', ' speed', '\n', '-', ' cost', '\n', '-', ' support']
NEW tokenized prompt tail: 
[... , '\n\n', '-', ' speed', '\n', '-', ' cost', '\n', '-', ' support']

ellie_support: customer notes that chat-template change removed a trailing "\n" in the system prompt, and the tokenizer normalization collapsed adjacent newlines which affected the assistant's internal formatting signal. They believe the model learned to rely on exact newline counts to trigger list formatting.

mike_eng: thanks — that matches a hypothesis. Two quick asks: (1) can you paste the exact system prompt we served for that customer (non-sensitive) and the request_id for a sample failing call? (2) can ML confirm whether list-formatting behavior is sensitive to newline token spacing for this model?

ellie_support: sample request_id: r-0a7c2f1b. System prompt (redacted): "You are a helpful assistant. Follow the user's formatting.\n" — note the single trailing newline used to be present, but template-trim removed it so now it's "You are a helpful assistant. Follow the user's formatting."

sara_ml: reproducing locally now against redwood-vicuna-1.2@stable-2026-03-15. Quick test shows that when tokenizer turns two consecutive newline codepoints into a single token "\n\n" -> "\n" we lose an explicit empty line that the LM seems to treat as list delimiter. Also include_eos_on_prompt=true appends an extra EOS token which moves list markers closer to EOS in the sequence. Both small shifts can flip top-1 decoding for a low-temp deterministic request.

sara_ml: reproduction snippet (local):
```py
prompt = "System: You are a helpful assistant. Follow the user's formatting.\n"
user = "List the top 3 reasons to prefer X over Y:\n- speed\n- cost\n- support"
# tokenized lengths
print(tok.len(prompt), tok.len(user))
# try with and without template trim and with include_eos_on_prompt toggled
```

jamal_prod: product question — is pinning customers to the pre-rollout model version an option while we triage? Can we expose a flag in the console to force old tokenizer/chat-template?

mike_eng: short-term we can do two things: (A) roll back the tokenizer normalization toggle on the affected runtime (commit abc123 revert) to restore exact newline tokenization, (B) add a shim in the chat runtime to append an explicit "\n" to system prompts for customers who observe regressions (quick config flip). Rolling back tokenizer globally is heavier but safest.

ellie_support: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — would prefer pin to old behavior. They are on Dedicated but using stable control plane.

deploy-bot: Deployment stable-2026-03-15 was applied to pool-a at 2026-03-15T02:12:34Z.

mike_eng: @deploy-bot can we patch pool-a only with tokenizer revert while leaving other pools on the new build? Need canary wedge.

deploy-bot: rollback job started for pool-a (job id rb-8894). ETA ~12m.

ellie_support: I informed ACME support contact (Ben) that we're investigating and initiated a pin request. He asked for repro steps to confirm once fixed.

sara_ml: action items: (1) I will run a focused diff of token IDs for the example and produce a one-pager showing sensitive token positions (2) Mike to coordinate pool-level rollback (3) Jamal to draft console pinning guidance and SOC message for customers.

mike_eng: will watch rb-8894 and post results. If rollback doesn't resolve, we may need to revert include_eos_on_prompt next.

deploy-bot: rollback rb-8894 completed on pool-a at 2026-03-15T02:23:10Z.

mike_eng: confirmed: quick smoke against r-0a7c2f1b request_id now returns bulleted list identical to pre-rollout. Closing immediate escalation.

ellie_support: passing to customer with summary + ask to verify on their side. Thanks all. :pray:
